characters.title: Characters
characters.subtitle: In the caverns beneath the world, even broken things remember how to protect.

list.name: Lanterne
list.tagline: An empty knight with a lantern-shaped head, no body, no voice, and a duty he does not understand.
list.description: Lanterne is not a legendary warrior. He is damaged, awkward, and strangely innocent, an old armor awakened in the depths of a blue cavern. He cannot truly speak. Only hollow metallic sounds, creaks, groans, and quiet gestures reveal what he feels. Yet when danger comes, he places himself between Rose and the world.

list.name: Rose
list.tagline: A quiet child whose presence makes life return where nothing should grow.
list.description: Rose is small, calm, and almost unreal. She walks through ruined places with a strange serenity, as if she can hear what the world has forgotten. Around her, flowers bloom, roots move, and the dead earth sometimes remembers how to breathe. But Rose is not a weapon, not a miracle to spend, and not a symbol. She is a child.

list.name: The Sleeping Machines
list.tagline: Colossal mechanical-organic beings, half dead, half dreaming beneath moss and roots.
list.description: Long after the old catastrophe, the machines still lie buried in the blue forests. Their bodies are rusted, cracked, and covered in fungi, but some eyes still open in the dark. They do not hate. They do not forgive. They awaken like forgotten disasters.

list.name: The Masked Pilgrims
list.tagline: Figures in black hoods and white masks, carrying strange rituals through the mist.
list.description: Seen only from afar, they move through the cavern platforms in silent processions. Their gongs echo across the abyss. Nobody knows if they are guardians, mourners, or something older. Their presence means the depths are not empty.

knights.title: The Thirteen Knights
knights.subtitle: A procession of hollow armors beneath the earth, from 13 to 1. Two faces are known; the rest will be revealed in coming episodes.
knights.hiddenTeaser: Their identity will be revealed in a coming episode.

12.name: Lanterne
12.title: The Silent Knight
12.tagline: He has no voice. No body. Only a child to protect.
12.description:
Lanterne is the 12th Knight, and one of the weakest among the thirteen.

He awakens alone on an ancient altar, animated by a strange blue energy. There is no body inside his armor. He cannot speak. He cannot write. He cannot explain who he is or what he remembers.

Around his neck, he carries a pendant showing the face of Rose, a mysterious Source Child connected to the human life he lost. When Rose is near, the pendant glows with blue light.

Lanterne is not a traditional hero. He stumbles, hesitates, falls, and observes the world with the fragile attention of someone who has forgotten how to exist.

But beneath his silence, something remains: warmth.

He may be one of the weakest knights, but he may also be the only one capable of protecting Rose without losing what makes him human.

9.name: Serrure
9.title: The Lock Knight
9.tagline: His kindness is real. His oath is dangerous.
9.description:
Serrure is the 9th Knight.

Unlike many of the other oath-bound knights, Serrure has not lost his warmth. He is gentle, welcoming, and strangely reassuring in a world where every knight could become a rival.

When Lanterne is weak, lost, and unable to understand the danger around him, Serrure becomes one of the first signs that not every knight is an enemy.

He speaks with kindness. He helps Lanterne understand the oath, the Source Children, and the path toward the Forgotten Garden.

But Serrure is not free.

Like every knight, he is bound to his own Source Child: Aren, a boy with red and white hair whose awakening closes the first episode.

Serrure's warmth makes him precious.
His oath makes him dangerous.
And one day, his kindness may be tested by the child he was waiting for.

hero.subtitle: An independent animated dark fantasy series from a one-person studio.

hero.emotional: In a forgotten underground world, a voiceless knight awakens with one certainty: he must find Rose.

humanCraft.label: Hybrid creation
humanCraft.text: Lost Garden is semi AI-assisted, under human direction. The screenplay was written by hand in ScreenWeaver, which made the work genuinely comfortable. Initial character concepts and sketches were drawn by Frank Houbre, then reworked for animation. Melodies were composed on guitar, then reworked and accompanied with AI.

storyAngle.title: Why Lost Garden is drawing attention
storyAngle.lead: Lost Garden is not a technical demonstration. It is a complete narrative episode with a world, characters, art direction, a soundtrack, and a deliberate pacing of scenes.
storyAngle.body: The project asks a concrete question of the creative industry: what happens to animated production when an independent creator can finally turn a personal vision into a full episode, without waiting for access to a studio, a team, or a traditional budget? Artificial intelligence is not presented here as a magic shortcut. It is part of a human-led creative pipeline: writing, breakdown, visual choices, continuity, editing, music, sound design, and finishing.

items.label: Writing, art direction, editing, and production

one.title: Episode 1 · The Awakening of the Lantern Knight
paragraphs: The first episode of Lost Garden follows Lanterne, a silent knight who wakes alone in a vast underground realm crossed by blue forests, ancient ruins, forgotten machines, and ghostly presences.
He does not speak. He does not yet understand what he has become. But a luminous medallion guides him toward Rose, a mysterious child whose memory seems tied to his own existence.
The episode lays the foundations of a dark fantasy series centered on memory, transmission, sacrifice, and the possibility of continuing to love in a world almost entirely lost.

two.title: Episode 2 · The King Beneath the Vault
paragraphs: Episode Two begins exactly where The Awakening of the Lantern Knight ended. Far beneath the earth, at the bottom of an immense forgotten cavern, Lanterne and Serrure are still looking for a way forward.

Something is wrong. Serrure realises that Lanterne has been badly damaged, and in a world where the knights are hollow beings of armour, ancient mechanisms, and forgotten purpose, repairing him is nothing like treating a wound.

The two knights travel deeper into the buried world in search of someone, or something, able to put Lanterne back together. Under the endless stone vaults, another part of the Lost Garden is waiting for them, with its own inhabitants, its own rules, and its own king.

audience.title: Audience reception
audience.intro: Released in early June, Lost Garden quickly moved beyond the frame of a simple AI experiment. Reactions focused on the quality of the world, the musical atmosphere, visual coherence, and the surprise of discovering a complete solo-produced episode.
comments: It's simply sublime, I loved it. Bravo and thank you for this beautiful moment.
Doesn't even look like AI. It's strong.
It's exceptional, it deserves so much more visibility.
The OST, the sound design… Several moments are so well done I forgot it was AI.
I just watched something this incredible for free? It's the first time I've been this absorbed by a world I knew nothing about from episode one.
Bravo, it's incredible. It really looks like animation from a proper studio. The story makes you want to see what comes next.

pressRelease.title: Press Release
pressRelease.headline: Independent creator completes solo 17-minute animated episode with AI-assisted production workflow
paragraphs: At a time when producing an animated series typically requires large teams, months of coordination, and substantial budgets, Frank Houbre presents Lost Garden, an independent animated dark fantasy series whose first episode was produced solo.
Running 17 minutes, this first episode was written, directed, edited, and finished by its creator using an AI-assisted production workflow.

Lost Garden unfolds in a vast underground world populated by silent knights, mysterious children, forgotten machines, and organic landscapes bathed in blue light. The story follows Lanterne, a fragile, mute knight guided by the memory of a child named Rose.
Since its release in early June, the episode has surpassed 65,000 views in just a few days, generating strong positive responses around its atmosphere, art direction, music, and narrative ambition.

The project does not rely on automatic generation. AI functions as a production tool within a human-led creative chain: writing, storyboard, staging, visual continuity, editing, sound design, and post-production.
With Lost Garden, Frank Houbre explores a new way to produce independent animation: lighter, more direct, yet always grounded in an author's vision.

The entire production runs on ScreenWeaver, the creative tool built by Frank Houbre. The screenplay was written there by hand, in a genuine writing environment that made the work comfortable and kept the script as the single source of truth. The storyboard was then generated in full by ScreenWeaver, scene by scene, from that screenplay. Finally, every shot was produced through its workflow and production interface. This research into new creative workflows extends directly from the experience of Lost Garden.
quotes: Lost Garden was not born from a magic button. It is a project written, directed, edited, and built step by step. AI allowed me to produce alone a vision that would normally have required an entire team.
I do not see these tools as a way to remove the human from creation. I see them as an opportunity for independent creators to finally tell stories too large for their usual means.

aboutFrank.title: About Frank Houbre
aboutFrank.bio: Frank Houbre is a French entrepreneur and creator specializing in new AI-assisted audiovisual workflows. His work sits at the intersection of storytelling, art direction, marketing, video production, and creative tools. With Lost Garden, he experiments with an extremely lean independent studio model, in which one person can write, visualize, produce, and finish a complete animated episode. He is also the creator of ScreenWeaver, the tool that connects writing, narrative structure, storyboard, and visual production, and the tool he used to write, storyboard, and produce all of Lost Garden.

quotes.title: Quotes
quotes.intro: Excerpts available for articles, interviews, and press materials.
items: Lost Garden began with a simple question: how far can a solo creator go when they finally have tools capable of keeping pace with their imagination?
AI did not write Lost Garden for me. It allowed me to produce the images, shots, and sequences needed to give form to a world I was already carrying.
What interests me is not replacing a studio. It is understanding how an independent creator can today build a complete narrative prototype that is visible, shareable, and emotionally legible.
I believe the next great worlds will not come only from large structures. Some will also come from solo creators able to prove their vision with a first episode.

game.headline: The Lantern's Oath
game.lead: A retro platformer under the earth, in the Lost Garden universe. Lanterne, twelfth of the thirteen knights, crosses one big map in eight zones: the blue forest, the ledges, the roots, the deep path, Serrure's tavern, the graveyard of machines. Dodge roll, charged glimmer, a light to hide, and the Machine at the end.
controls: Arrow keys or A / D: move
Z, W, Space or Up: jump (release early for a short hop)
Down: crouch, ducks under the Machine's beam
Down + jump: drop through a platform
X, K or Enter: throw the glimmer (crouched or Down: throw low)
Hold X after a throw, then release: charged glimmer, 3 damage, pierces
C, L or Shift: dodge roll, invulnerable while rolling
Esc or P: pause and options (music, effects, language)
game.touchHint: On a phone, use the on-screen buttons.
lore: One big map, eight zones in a row: the Waking, the Ledges, the Descent of the Roots, the Pilgrims' Gong, the Deep Path, Serrure's Tavern, the Graveyard of Machines, the Arena.

The Pack: wolf-shaped masses of ash that sleep by the deep paths and throw themselves at any light. Crouched, your lantern hides: you can slip past. A charged glimmer on a sleeping beast hits twice as hard.
The Sleepers: cocooned in the roots. A blow or a lingering light wakes them; they are slow but tough. Ash moths fly to your lantern. Glowing beetles crawl the ground: throw low or stomp them.

The Scaled Ones watch from the shadows and vanish when approached: they are not enemies. The polite jellyfish of the pit serve as platforms. The roots of the Source Tree break through the moss after a tremor.

The pilgrims' gong and Serrure's tavern mend the armour and serve as checkpoints. At Serrure's, three lilies are worth a heart. The Machine, at the end of the graveyard, stomps, fires a beam and calls the beetles at half health.

In the graveyard of machines a colossus wakes: it is a run. Sprint without looking back, jump the walls and the gaps, dodge the claws that slam down ahead of you, and drop into the arena where it cannot follow. The Machine waits for you there.
Esc opens the in-game options: music, sound effects, language (French or English), controls. Three hits and the armour sinks into the moss. Lanterne never speaks.

The soundtrack is the series' own, composed by Frank Houbre: Ash Lantern Prayer in the forest, Song of the Empty Sky in the roots, The Giant and the Knight on the deep path and during the run, The Knight's Lullaby at Serrure's, Inexorable Ascent in the graveyard, Clockwork Requiem against the Machine.
game.credits: An original game for the anime Lost Garden by Frank Houbre. No download, no account, plays in the browser.
